title: Investigating OpenAI’s ChatGPT Potentials in Generating Chatbot's Dialogue for English as a Foreign Language Learning
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT can generate suitable reference dialogues for an English as a Foreign Language (EFL) chatbot system. The central question is not whether ChatGPT improves learning outcomes in a live classroom trial, but whether its generated dialogue content is readable and appropriate for learners at different proficiency levels. The authors argue that dialogue quality matters for chatbot-based language learning because students need materials that are understandable, varied, and not overly complex.

The study uses ChatGPT to generate dialogue pairs for a mobile voice-enabled chatbot intended to support EFL speaking practice. The prompt specifies a conversation between an undergraduate student at Tokyo Denki University and an exchange student from Italy, and the model is also asked to produce alternative lines for each dialogue turn. In total, 450 dialogue combinations are analyzed. The evaluation relies on three readability measures: Flesch Reading Ease, Dale-Chall, and McAlpine EFLAW, which together are used to judge text difficulty from different angles.

The paper concludes that most ChatGPT-generated dialogues fall in a range suitable for CEFR A2 learners, with some materials also providing challenge for B1 learners. The dialogues are generally easy to understand and contain few mini-words or other features likely to confuse EFL readers. The authors suggest that ChatGPT has promise as a low-cost content-generation tool for chatbot dialogue creation, especially for mobile EFL applications, though higher-level learners may find the materials too simple.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed empirical paper, but it is primarily a descriptive readability analysis rather than a controlled experiment or quasi-experiment. It provides systematic measurement of generated text, yet it does not evaluate learner outcomes or compare interventions under a rigorous causal design.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests practical usefulness for EFL dialogue generation, but the impact is indirect and unmeasured with students. Because no effect size on learning or engagement is reported, the demonstrated impact on learners is modest and unclear.

interventions.use_case: Using ChatGPT to generate reference dialogue lines and alternative replies for an EFL chatbot mobile application; the dialogues are intended to support speaking, listening, and reading practice for learners.

A mobile voice-enabled chatbot app that loads ChatGPT-generated reference dialogues, plays the first line via text-to-speech, and supports read-aloud practice with speech recognition-based pronunciation checking.

finding.finding_summary: Across 450 ChatGPT-generated dialogue samples, the text was judged suitable for EFL speaking practice, especially for CEFR A2 learners. Most dialogues scored in the Flesch Reading Ease 80-90 range and were interpreted as easily comprehensible for sixth-grade elementary students, with some content also stretching B1 learners. No experimental learning gain was measured; the paper’s claim is about readability-based suitability rather than student performance.
finding.measure: Readability metrics applied to generated dialogue text (Flesch Reading Ease, Dale-Chall, McAlpine EFLAW)

finding.finding_summary: The study evaluated whether ChatGPT-generated dialogues were linguistically appropriate as instructional reading material for EFL learners. Based on Dale-Chall and McAlpine EFLAW, the dialogue set was generally easy to understand and avoided many mini-words/wordy expressions that can confuse international readers, suggesting favorable literacy-level accessibility for A2-B1 learners.
finding.measure: Readability metrics of written dialogue content

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that ChatGPT could reduce the time and effort needed for teachers or developers to create reference dialogues for a chatbot, since the model can generate multiple topics and alternative lines automatically. This is a conceptual efficiency claim supported by the successful generation of 450 dialogue combinations, not a measured workload comparison.
finding.measure: Dialogue generation feasibility / author-described reduction in content creation effort
